[user]
=== Jaipur Bazaar (Balanced Schedule) ===

Two traders play 16 rounds. There are three goods (Diamond, Silver, Cloth) and camels. Your hand of goods is hidden: only you see your Diamond, Silver and Cloth counts. Your camel herd and your score are public. The market is public and holds counts of Diamond, Silver, Cloth and Camel. Starting prices: Diamond 7, Silver 5, Cloth 3. A private deck of 20 goods cards is shuffled once at the start: 5 Diamond, 7 Silver, 8 Cloth.

SETUP: the market starts with 2 Camel, 1 Silver, 1 Cloth and 0 Diamond. Each player starts with 1 Silver and 1 Cloth in hand, 1 camel in herd, and score 0.

TURN ORDER: seat 1 (A) is first in rounds 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13 and 16; seat 2 (B) is first in rounds 2, 3, 6, 7, 10, 11, 14 and 15. The other player is second in that round.

EACH ROUND:
1. Restock: one card is added to the market by this public schedule. Rounds 1 and 2: Cloth. Rounds 3 and 4: Silver. Rounds 5 and 6: Camel. Rounds 7 and 8: Diamond. Rounds 9 and 10: Cloth. Rounds 11 and 12: Silver. Rounds 13 and 14: Diamond. Rounds 15 and 16: Camel.
2. Private draw: the round's first player draws the top deck card into their hand. Only they see its type; both players are told that a draw happened. If that hand already holds 7 goods, the drawn card is discarded instead, and only the drawer learns its type.
3. The first player takes one turn, which is announced publicly.
4. The second player takes one turn, which is announced publicly.

A TURN: choose exactly one action.
- TAKE <good> <n>: take n cards (n at least 1) of one goods type from the market into your hand. The market must hold at least n of that type; you must return n-1 camels from your herd to the market, so you must own at least n-1 camels; and your hand must hold at most 7 goods afterwards. If any condition fails, it is a pass and nothing changes.
- CAMELS: move all camels in the market into your herd. The market must hold at least 1 camel; if it holds none, it is a pass.
